items.title: docs(adr): registra as decisões-chave em MADR
items.body: ## Resumo Registra as decisões de arquitetura do Megila em `docs/adr/`, no formato MADR 4.0.0 e em português. Cada ADR tem contexto e problema, opções consideradas, decisão e consequências. O índice lista as seis. `template.md` é o modelo das próximas. ## Decisões - **0001.** Python na orquestração. Whisper (CTranslate2) e ffmpeg/libx264 já são C/C++; Rust não encurta esse caminho. - **0002.** Licença MIT, sem código AGPL, GPL ou SSPL. SupoClip fica só como ideia de produto (cortes curtos), nunca como código. - **0003.** Fila própria em SQLite com WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, lease com token, heartbeat, DLQ no status `dead` e checkpoint por pedaço com SHA-256. - **0004.** Qualidade antes da velocidade: faster-whisper `large-v3` `int8`, x264 preset `slow` CRF 19, overlays ASS compilados pelo Megila, resumo em várias passagens sem molde, gates de VMAF que falham fechado. - **0005.** Modelo de texto plugável, local por padrão. Chave externa só no keyring do sistema, nunca em log, fila ou arquivo de configuração. - **0006.** Processamento e armazenamento locais. Backup com rclone (Drive é um remote possível) e worker remoto (Colab ou outra máquina) são opt-in. O worker não abre o SQLite. `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` e `mkdocs.yml` não foram alterados. ## Linha para o CHANGELOG Na seção de adições: ```markdown - ADRs 0001 a 0006 em `docs/adr/`, no formato MADR, com índice e modelo para decisões novas. ``` ## Entrada de nav para o MkDocs Com `docs_dir: docs`: ```yaml - Decisões arquiteturais: adr/index.md ``` ## Validação `npx --yes markdownlint-cli@0.50.0 --config docs/adr/.markdownlint.yaml "docs/adr/**/*.md"` terminou sem erro. Nenhum serviço pago foi usado.

items.title: fix(preflight): say a source may be live when its length can't be verified
items.body:
## Problem

On Nov 10 one user tried to create a task from an active YouTube live stream 13 times. For an active stream, the YouTube Data API reports `duration: P0D`. `get_youtube_video_info` returned that zero without trying the other provider. The preflight then showed the generic `503 VIDEO_METADATA_UNAVAILABLE` ("try again shortly"), so retrying was the obvious next step. No minutes were charged.

## Approach

This PR decides on **length only**. It does not detect live status, so it never tells a user that a video *is* live. When a provider answers but gives no positive length, after the bounded fallback below, the user gets:

> We couldn't verify this {YouTube|Twitch|Kick} video's length. It may be a livestream that's still in progress, which isn't supported yet. If it's a finished video, try again shortly; otherwise wait until the stream ends and use the completed recording. No minutes were used.

The response is `422 VIDEO_DURATION_UNAVAILABLE`, with the usual `{code, message}` detail. No task is created, no job is queued and no minutes are charged.

### YouTube (`youtube_utils.py`, `api/routes/tasks.py`)
- If a metadata provider returns no positive length, the other provider gets **one** try under the existing preflight deadline. This is metadata only and downloads nothing. If neither returns a length, the first result is returned and the preflight gives the 422 above.
- If no provider answers at all (exceptions, nothing returned), the response is still `503 VIDEO_METADATA_UNAVAILABLE`. Timeout and geo-restriction keep their existing codes.

### Twitch / Kick (`stream_source.py`, `api/routes/tasks.py`)
- `fetch_stream_info` already moves through its bounded chain: yt-dlp proxy and direct, then the cheap metadata actor. It never runs parsebird. It now records whether any provider *answered without a length*. If no provider produced a length, it raises `StreamDurationUnavailableError`, a subclass of `StreamSourceError`, and the route turns that into the 422 above.
- If every provider simply failed, the response is still `422 VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE` ("couldn't fetch"). Private and subscriber-only VODs keep their message. Channel links are still rejected by `detect_stream_source` before any metadata call.

### Unchanged
- A positive length goes through the plan cap (`VIDEO_TOO_LONG`), the billing check sized to that length, and task creation exactly as before.

## Web / iOS

There are no client changes. The web create proxy passes `detail` through, and `normalizeMessage` shows `detail.message`. iOS should show the message the same way it does for the other 422 preflight codes. I couldn't check that because the app's source isn't in this repo.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/test_duration_unavailable_preflight.py`, with every provider mocked:
  - **YouTube:** a zero length falls back and succeeds; a valid first result never calls the fallback; zero plus zero, or zero plus an error, gives one call each and an unverified result; all providers failing still returns `None`.
  - **YouTube task creation:** the incident path (yt-dlp gives no length, the Data API gives `P0D`) returns the 422 with the "may be a livestream" message; a fetch failure still returns the 503; a positive length is billed for that length; the plan cap still applies.
  - **Twitch and Kick:** a zero or missing length from every provider gives `StreamDurationUnavailableError`, with at most one cheap actor run and never parsebird; zero from yt-dlp then an actor success is billed normally; provider failures stay plain fetch failures; a positive length from the first provider runs no actor.
  - **Twitch/Kick task creation:** the 422 message for each platform; a fetch failure stays `VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE`; a positive length is billed; the plan cap still applies; a channel link is rejected before any metadata call.
  - Every rejection case asserts there was no task, no enqueue and no billing check sized to a duration.
- `test_task_duration_preflight.py`: no metadata at all gives a 503; metadata without a usable length (`{}`, `None`, `0`, `-1`, `NaN`, `True`) gives a 422.
- `test_youtube_utils.py`: the provider-selection mocks now carry a real duration, so "fallback should not run" still means what it says.
- Full `tests/unit` run (backend image, disposable Redis): **2608 passed, 4 failed, 9 skipped**. The same 4 fail on `origin/main`: `test_source_identity::test_duplicate_copy_is_translated_in_every_app_language`, two in `test_video_cleanup`, and `test_workflow_notes_contract::test_the_scan_sees_the_planners`.
- I didn't run the integration tests, because they need Postgres.

## Limitations

- A live Twitch or Kick VOD that reports a **positive, growing** length isn't caught. It goes through the normal path, as it does today. This PR only covers sources whose length is zero or missing.
- A finished video whose providers all briefly report no length gets the "may be a livestream" message instead of a plain "try again". The message suggests retrying for that reason.
- Other callers of `get_youtube_video_info` (the worker and the Apify quality cap) also get the one extra metadata try when the first provider returns no length.

items.title: Add Mission Control hub gateway and clip skill infrastructure
items.body:
## Summary

This PR introduces two major new systems to the SupoClip ecosystem:

1. **Mission Control Hub Gateway** — A lightweight federated tool hub that aggregates status, news, and market data from multiple independent services (SupoClip, Flowsint, MiroFish, changedetection.io, RSSHub, etc.) into a single dashboard.

2. **Clip Skill** — A comprehensive AI video clipper skill system with modular scripts for downloading, transcribing, analyzing, cutting, stitching, and publishing clips.

## Key Changes

### Hub Gateway (`hub/gateway/`)
- **`main.py`** — FastAPI service exposing:
  - `/api/modules` — Module registry from `modules.json`
  - `/api/status` — Live health checks of all registered services
  - `/api/news` — Aggregated RSS/Atom feed items with caching
  - `/api/markets` — Polymarket/Kalshi prediction market data with 24h deltas
  - `/api/events` — Alert log from the watcher
  - `/` — Static dashboard
- **`watcher.py`** — Background asyncio loop that monitors markets and HN, fires alerts via ntfy push notifications based on configurable rules (market moves, HN points, keyword matching)
- **`history.py`** — SQLite-backed market snapshot history for change-over-time tracking
- **Dashboard** (`dashboard/`) — Single-page app with:
  - Module cards showing live service health
  - News feed aggregation
  - Prediction markets browser with 24h volume/delta
  - Clip library panel
  - Real-time status pill and briefing section
- **`modules.json`** — Registry of hub modules with health URLs and metadata
- **Docker Compose** (`docker-compose.hub.yml`) — Orchestrates gateway, changedetection.io, RSSHub, and ntfy
- **Makefile** — Commands to setup vendored modules, start/stop services

### Clip Skill (`.claude/skills/clip/`)
- **`SKILL.md`** — Comprehensive documentation of the clip pipeline and agent workflow
- **`scripts/download.py`** — Download videos from 1800+ sites (YouTube, Twitch, Kick, etc.) via yt-dlp
- **`scripts/transcribe.py`** — Word-level transcription with faster-whisper, WhisperX, or AssemblyAI
- **`scripts/cut_clip.py`** — Core clip generation with:
  - 9:16 vertical framing with face-centered crop (MediaPipe → OpenCV → Haar cascade fallback)
  - Word-synced karaoke captions in 5 templates (default, hormozi, mrbeast, minimal, tiktok)
  - Platform export presets (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) with matching bitrates
  - B-roll overlay support
  - Optional static hook title
- **`scripts/transcribe.py`** — Multi-engine transcription (faster-whisper, WhisperX with diarization, AssemblyAI)
- **`scripts/stitch.py`** — Concatenate clips with optional crossfade or stinger transitions
- **`scripts/publish.py`** — Publish clips to YouTube Shorts or via webhook (n8n/Zapier integration)
- **`scripts/library.py`** — Register finished clips into the shared library that the hub dashboard reads
- **`scripts/broll.py`** — Fetch stock footage from Pexels API
- **`scripts/render.py`** — Render segments into vertical clips with captions

### Hub Infrastructure
- **`hub/README.md`** — Architecture overview and module descriptions
- **`hub/setup.sh`** — Clone/update vendored modules (Flowsint, MiroFish, Firecrawl, Perplexica)
- **`.gitignore`** — Ignore `.clips/` directory and gateway history DB

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Health checks** use configurable `{host}` placeholder (localhost for direct run, `host.docker.internal` in Docker) to reach services on the host
